_note: Voice bake-off v2. Calm, intriguing delivery (never loud), General American accents. See docs/VOICE.md for the evidence behind these choices. [tags] are only used by Chatterbox Turbo; other engines strip them.

designs.a: Male voice, late twenties, General American accent. Warm, smooth, low-mid pitch with a slightly breathy, intimate quality, like a curious storyteller letting you in on a secret. Calm and never loud. Wide, expressive intonation, natural pauses, a hint of a smile. Confident and relaxed; not nasal, not whiny, no stammering.
designs.b: Male voice, about thirty, General American accent. Rich, slightly husky voice leaning toward baritone, relaxed and assured, like a late-night podcast host who finds everything fascinating. Soft-spoken and intriguing, clear diction, playful curiosity, never shouting. Not nasal, not high-pitched.

kip.reference_text: So here's the thing. Every day I find out the real story behind something we see all the time... and honestly? It never gets old. Let's see what today's is.

designs.a: Male voice, late thirties, General American accent. Low, calm, velvety baritone with a dry deadpan wit. Slow, measured and precise, quietly amused, never loud. Smooth and understated.
designs.b: Male voice, about forty, General American accent. Deep, soft, slightly gravelly voice, unhurried and understated, like a museum curator sharing something he finds quietly delightful. Dry, warm, a little sardonic.

dex.reference_text: This is Dex. I check the facts, I bring the sources, and I try very hard not to be impressed. Today... I will probably fail at that.

intrigued.instruct: intrigued and curious, drawing the listener in, calm, with rising interest

hushed.instruct: hushed and conspiratorial, almost whispering, as if sharing a secret

stunned.instruct: quietly stunned, breathless disbelief, slow, not loud

amused.instruct: softly amused, a small warm laugh, delighted

dry.instruct: dry and wry, with a tired, slightly amused sigh

lines.speaker: kip
lines.text: Here's something strange. The lead in your pencil... isn't lead. Not even a little.

lines.speaker: dex
lines.text: It's graphite, mixed with clay. People just mistook it for lead. Two sources, Kip.

lines.speaker: kip
lines.text: [gasp] Wait... so we've been calling it the wrong thing... for centuries?

lines.speaker: kip
lines.text: And here's the part nobody tells you.

lines.speaker: kip
lines.text: [chuckle] Okay. That's actually kind of amazing.

lines.speaker: dex
lines.text: [sigh] You say that every single day.
